# Results — Study 616 (Muni-CEF-Tax-Loss)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Starks, Yong & Zheng 2006, JF) — **municipal-bond closed-end funds get dumped for tax losses
in December, widening their discounts, and snap back in January** — tested on a fixed
**12-fund seasoned muni CEF panel** against **MUB** (the NAV-priced muni ETF), with the
fund-minus-benchmark **excess total return as the discount-motion proxy**. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `5f10f3e3801d`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes — 12 seasoned national muni CEFs (NEA, NVG, NZF, NUV, NXP, BTT, MYI, MQY, MHD, EIM, VMO, MMU) + benchmarks MUB & VWLTX (public, no key) |
| Window | 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (6,662 rows); MUB-excess panel **2007-10 → 2026-06** (225 months, **19 winters** Dec 2007 → Jan 2026); VWLTX-excess extends to **26 winters** (2000 →) |
| Discount proxy | fund monthly total return **minus** benchmark monthly total return — the benchmark prices at NAV, so negative excess = the CEF's price lagging the muni market (discount widening); both legs total-return, so the CEFs' monthly distributions don't pollute the seasonal comparison |
| Execution / costs | the signal is a **fixed calendar rule** (knowable arbitrarily in advance); every entry/exit fills at the first close **after** its decision point (month-boundary or mid-month date) — the single execution lag; swap trade charged **4 one-way legs × 5/10/25 bps × NAV** per winter |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The panel is 12 muni CEFs *still trading* in
> 2026 — merged or liquidated funds (BFK and MYD, for instance, are already gone from the
> tape) cannot appear. For a seasonal test the bias is milder than for a level edge (a fund's
> survival doesn't obviously depend on its Decembers), but a surviving panel is a healthier,
> more-owned panel — which is exactly the clientele the tax-loss story needs — so the
> magnitude may tilt up. *Opt-in guard:* swap `FUNDS` for a point-in-time muni-CEF list.

## Pooled fund-months (secondary — pseudo-replication caveat)

All muni CEFs move together within a calendar month, so pooling fund-months overstates the
effective sample; these Welch *t*'s are quoted as **secondary** evidence only.

| bucket | mean excess (bps/mo) | n | Welch *t* vs rest |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| December | **−13.05** | 228 | −0.88 |
| January | **+186.27** | 228 | **+6.57** |
| other months | +3.52 | 2,244 | — |
| January vs December | — | — | **+6.10** |

## The primary test — per-winter basket (one observation per winter)

Equal-weight the panel each month, then take **one December and one January number per
winter** — the conservative unit that kills the cross-fund pseudo-replication. One-sample *t*
across 19 non-overlapping winters (snap lag-1 autocorrelation **+0.069** — plain *t* is
appropriate on annual data).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| winters | 19 (Dec 2007 → Jan 2026) |
| December excess | **−15.75 bps** · *t* = **−0.33** |
| **January excess** | **+191.25 bps** · *t* = **+2.27** · hit rate **84.2%** |
| snap-back (Jan − Dec) | **+207.00 bps** · *t* = **+1.83** · hit rate **73.7%** |

The claim splits cleanly in two. The **January snap-back is real**: +191 bps of excess over
MUB in the average January, positive in 16 of 19 winters, one-sample *t* = 2.27 — over the
desk bar. The **December-month dump is not there** at monthly grain: −16 bps, *t* = −0.33.
(The third axis below shows why: the dump and the start of the recovery both live *inside*
December — the calendar month nets them out.)

## Exact seasonal placebo — all 132 ordered month pairs (no RNG)

Could a random pair of months look this special? We enumerate **every** ordered pair of
distinct calendar months (a, b) and compute the basket's seasonal mean(b) − mean(a).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed Dec→Jan contrast | **+207.00 bps** |
| rank among 132 ordered pairs | **4** |
| exact *p* | **0.0303** (minimum attainable 1/132 = 0.0076) |

Dec→Jan sits in the top 3% of all month-pair contrasts — and the pairs that beat it all
involve January or February (January is the panel's best month, February its worst: the
snap-back partially gives back). The adjacent-pair grid (bps): Jan→Feb **−245**, …,
Oct→Nov +160, Nov→Dec −90, **Dec→Jan +207** — the seasonal structure is exactly the tax-loss
calendar's shape.

## Robustness — VWLTX benchmark, full 2000+ history (26 winters)

MUB only lists in 2007. VWLTX (Vanguard Long-Term Tax-Exempt, NAV-priced) extends the same
test to 26 winters:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| winters | 26 |
| January excess | **+180.34 bps** · *t* = **+3.51** · hit rate **88.5%** |
| December excess | +16.31 bps · *t* = +0.49 |
| snap-back (Jan − Dec) | **+164.03 bps** · *t* = **+2.73** |
| exact placebo *p* | **0.0455** (rank 6/132) |

Same picture, more power: January real (*t* = 3.51), December flat.

## Sub-period fade (midpoint split, not snooped)

| sample | January excess (bps) | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| MUB 2007–2016 | **+326.63** | +2.56 | 10 |
| MUB 2017–2025 | **+40.83** | +0.45 | 9 |
| VWLTX 2000–2012 | **+274.92** | +3.72 | 13 |
| VWLTX 2013–2025 | **+85.76** | +1.34 | 13 |

The January effect is concentrated in the first half of the sample on **both** benchmarks.
The Welch *t* of the early-minus-late difference is **+1.83** — the fade itself is *not*
certified at *t* ≥ 2, but the recent decade alone cannot certify the effect either. This is a
McLean-Pontiff-shaped decay pattern (the anomaly was published in 2006) and it drives the
Tradability stamp.

## Costs — the January swap (hold MUB, swap into the basket for January)

Enter at the last December close, exit at the last January close; **4 one-way legs** per
winter (sell MUB, buy basket, sell basket, buy MUB) at one-way cost × NAV. Gross P&L over
just-holding-MUB is exactly the basket's January excess.

| one-way cost | drag (bps) | gross (bps/winter) | net (bps/winter) | *t* net | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | 20 | +191.25 | **+171.25** | **+2.03** | 84.2% |
| 10 bps | 40 | +191.25 | **+151.25** | +1.79 | 78.9% |
| 25 bps | 100 | +191.25 | **+91.25** | +1.08 | 73.7% |

At 5 bps the net swap still clears *t* = 2; at a realistic 10 bps one-way for small CEFs
(half-spreads alone often reach that) it slips to *t* = 1.79, and at 25 bps to 1.08. Add the
post-2016 gross of **+41 bps** — *below* the 40–100 bps cost drag — and the trade's last
decade is net-negative. Capacity: these funds average a few $100M with thin daily volume — a
few $100k moves the January price. Real premium historically; fragile vehicle now.

## Third axis — does buying Dec-15 beat buying Jan-15? (the actionable version)

Entry A = first close on/after **Dec-15**; entry B = first close on/after **Jan-15**; common
exit = last February close. The paired per-winter difference is exactly the excess earned
between Dec-15 and Jan-15 — i.e. does the snap-back start *before* year-end (so you must buy
into the December dump) or can you wait until mid-January?

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Dec-15 entry, excess to end-Feb | **+267.92 bps** |
| Jan-15 entry, excess to end-Feb | **+33.46 bps** |
| paired difference (Dec-15 − Jan-15) | **+234.45 bps** · *t* = **+1.78** · hit **73.7%** |
| ex-2008 (the outlier winter) | **+114.21 bps** · *t* = **+2.02** (n = 18) |

Directionally decisive: **almost the entire seasonal payoff lives between Dec-15 and
Jan-15** — by mid-January it's over (+33 bps left). Buying into the December dump is the
actionable version, positive in 14 of 19 winters; but the full-sample *t* = 1.78 leans on the
2008 winter (+24% excess), and ex-2008 it is +114 bps at *t* = 2.02 — right at the bar.
**MIXED**: the timing shape is clearly front-loaded, but 19 winters can't certify the Dec-15
edge beyond doubt.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

On a deterministic monthly excess panel (common muni-CEF factor + fund noise) with plantable
December-dump / January-snap knobs:

| planted (dump, snap) | Jan (bps) | *t* Jan | snap (bps) | *t* snap | exact placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **(0, 0)** — seasonally dead | +24.8 | +0.65 | +22.2 | +0.53 | 0.2424 |
| **(100, 100) bps** | +124.8 | **+3.26** | +222.2 | **+5.33** | **0.0076** |

Zero planted seasonality does not fire (*t* ≈ 0.6, placebo p = 0.24); planted knobs light up
(*t* = 5.3, placebo at its 1/132 floor). *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (*Real on the January snap-back · None on the December-month dump*).
  January excess over MUB is **+191 bps** at *t* = **2.27** (19 winters, hit 84%), **+180
  bps** at *t* = **3.51** on the 26-winter VWLTX tape, exact 132-pair placebo *p* =
  0.030/0.045 — the January leg clears the bar on both benchmarks. The December calendar
  month, however, is flat (−16 bps, *t* = −0.33): the dump and the start of the recovery net
  out inside December. Carries the **survivorship** caveat (a 12-survivor panel) and a named
  **fade** (post-2016 January = +41 bps, *t* = 0.45; the fade difference itself Welch *t* =
  1.83, not certified).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The January swap nets **+171 bps/winter at *t* = 2.03** at 5 bps
  one-way but slips under the bar at a realistic 10 bps (*t* = 1.79), the post-2016 gross
  (+41 bps) is *below* the 40–100 bps cost drag, it fires **once a year** on tiny,
  thin-volume funds (capacity a few $100k), and the effect is fading post-publication. Real
  historically, barely bankable now.
- **"Buy Dec-15, not Jan-15"? — MIXED.** Nearly all of the seasonal payoff sits between
  Dec-15 and Jan-15 (**+234 bps** paired difference, hit 74%; Jan-15 entry keeps only +33
  bps) — but the certification is borderline (*t* = 1.78 full sample; +114 bps at *t* = 2.02
  ex-2008). Directionally confirmed, statistically not sealed.
